source.section: Pub 120 PDF page 2 'What retirement income may I subtract', PDF page 3 'What federally taxed income may I not subtract'; Form IL-1040 Line 5; Instructions PDF page 7, Line 5; Form IL-1040 PDF page 1, Lines 1-19; Instructions PDF page 8, Lines 10-12; rate Instructions PDF page 1; Line 10a chart and Income Exceptions, Instructions PDF page 8

worked: Federal AGI = private pension (person 0) 50,000.00 + IRA distribution (person 0) 20,000.00 = 70,000.00. Federal taxable income = 70,000.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 - additional amount for 1 person(s) 65 or older 2,000.00 = 52,250.00 (federal senior deduction ignored; federal figures are given, not tested; Illinois starts from federal AGI). Form IL-1040 Line 1 federal AGI 70,000.00. Line 2 federally tax-exempt interest 0.00. Line 3 other additions 0.00. Line 4 = 70,000.00. Line 5 private pension 50,000.00 + IRA distribution 20,000.00 = 70,000.00. Lines 6 and 7 0.00. Line 8 = 70,000.00. Line 9 base income = 70,000.00 - 70,000.00 = 0.00. Income Exceptions: federal AGI 70,000.00 is not greater than 250,000.00, so the allowance stands. Line 10a 2,850.00. Line 10b 1,000.00 (1 box(es) x 1,000.00). Lines 10c and 10d 0.00. Line 10 = 3,850.00. Line 11 net income = 0.00 - 3,850.00 = -3,850.00, entered as 0.00 (the line may not be less than zero). Line 12 tax = 0.00 x 4.95% = 0.0000. Lines 13-18 0.00 (no credits in the projection). Line 19 state income tax = 0.00.
